name: 11396-repeatedimage-qwen2vl7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node (--gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
architecture: Qwen2VLForConditionalGeneration, bf16, 8.3B: 28-layer decoder (hidden 3584, 28 query heads over 4 KV heads) behind a 32-block vision tower, patch 14, spatial merge 2, 32768-token context.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=16, bounded at 1600 requests with an 1800 s safety cap, warmup the first 25% and cooldown the last 10% by completion.
workload: Single-image visual question answering over a fixed catalogue: 32 distinct 1280x720 JPEGs and 1600 requests walking them round robin, so each picture is sent 50 times. 1212 prompt tokens of which 1196 are the image, 20 tokens out.
purpose: A seven-billion-parameter vision assistant answering short questions about a 32-image product catalogue, 16 concurrent requests, one GPU.
launch:
# vLLM at commit 5ce4627a7ec4cf4e19ff4be7f030883ef486393f (`git describe --tags --match 'v*'` =
# v0.6.6.post1-5-g5ce4627a7ec4), on 1x H100 80GB HBM3. Any flag not listed is an engine default.

model: Qwen/Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16

# 1212 prompt tokens plus 20 generated, so 4096 clears the longest request with room to spare.
max-model-len: 4096

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
enable-prefix-caching: false

# Bring-up, not a tuning knob. Two keys, and NEITHER changes a single request this workload
# sends -- verified in the arm's own venv by driving a real pool JPEG through
# `InputPreprocessor.preprocess`: with and without them the result is identical, 1212
# `input_ids`, `pixel_values` (4784, 1176), grid [1, 52, 92].
#
#   use_fast    Era pin. The installed `transformers` (4.57.6) returns
#               `Qwen2VLImageProcessorFast`, while this engine's Qwen2-VL model file asserts the
#               legacy `Qwen2VLImageProcessor`; without it that bare assertion fires during
#               startup and the engine never comes up. It selects the processor CLASS only.
#
#   max_pixels  Caps the WORST CASE the engine budgets for, not the images. Left at the
#               checkpoint's own 12845056, `get_max_multimodal_tokens` returns 32768, so startup
#               profiling builds a synthetic sequence of ~16400 tokens -- one 12.8-megapixel image
#               through the vision tower -- against a `max-model-len` of 4096, and the engine
#               build dies there with no message and is retried forever. At 1003520 the same
#               call returns 2450 and the profiling batch becomes four realistic sequences.
#               A 1280x720 image smart_resizes to 1288x728 = 937664 pixels, UNDER this ceiling,
#               so the clamp is a no-op on every request actually sent.
#
# Must stay ONE line of JSON: the launcher's flat YAML reader skips indented continuations and
# would drop a block mapping silently.
mm-processor-kwargs: {"use_fast": false, "max_pixels": 1003520}
